purpose: The small, transparent, preregistered set of hindsight oracle exit rules FT2-05 will REPLAY to compute label-side opportunity ceilings. These are ceiling references, never learned policies and never entry targets.

canonical_intent_fill_recheck_law.authority: sole arithmetic and sequencing authority for D48/D49 decision-time intent eligibility and selected-contract fill-time recheck

serial_semantics.entry_commit_and_fill: BUY committed at completed t reserves the one position slot; cash/premium uses executable ask at e=t+1
serial_semantics.exit_decision_and_fill: EXIT decided at completed v fills at x=v+1 executable bid; occupancy releases at x
serial_semantics.occupancy_release: at the separately persisted realized t+1 exit-fill minute
serial_semantics.no_bid_forced_flat: actual 15:55 boundary state only; no earlier-bid substitution; no executable bid means $0 option value
serial_semantics.boundary_nonduplication: a committed 15:54 EXIT fills once at 15:55 and suppresses a second forced-flat valuation

census_layer_constraints.session_start_equity_E: account equity carried into the session under v5 within-split compounding; the 5% cap and 5% budget both scale off E

D48_per_trade_premium_cap.rule: decision-time intent eligibility at completed minute t is defined only by canonical_intent_fill_recheck_law.json:/decision_time_intent using information through t
D48_per_trade_premium_cap.effect: contracts failing the causal time-t intent mask are outside the oracle choice universe; the oracle may not use the future t+1 ask to restore or remove a decision-time action
D48_per_trade_premium_cap.fill_outcome: after one exact identity is committed, canonical_intent_fill_recheck_law.json:/fill_time_recheck determines pass or rejection at t+1
D48_per_trade_premium_cap.same_game: the exact referenced law hash must govern census, simulator, model, shadow, and live guard; restated arithmetic or a local override is forbidden

D49_budget_aware_entry.rule: decision-time budget intent legality at completed minute t is defined only by canonical_intent_fill_recheck_law.json:/decision_time_intent and the causal policy ledger
D49_budget_aware_entry.realized_session_loss: L = max(0, -(realized net PnL so far this session)); grows only as realized losing exits accumulate
D49_budget_aware_entry.effect: as L grows the causal time-t eligible ladder narrows; the fee-path-specific current-ladder soft-close predicate is owned by canonical_intent_fill_recheck_law.json:/soft_close
D49_budget_aware_entry.fill_outcome: only the committed exact identity is rechecked at t+1 under the referenced canonical law; rejection is not retroactive decision-time ineligibility

census_layer_constraints.daily_breaker: once L >= 0.05 * E the session takes no further entries (breaker keeps its signed realized-only basis; unchanged by these rules)

oracle_sequencing.principle: an oracle may rank future realized outcomes only after the causal time-t intent universe is frozen. It may never use t+1 availability, price, or recheck result to redefine the time-t universe. One-position occupancy, t<15:30 entry decisions, the 15:55 forced-flat boundary, and the 5% daily breaker remain binding.
oracle_sequencing.serial_ceiling_replay: iterate sessions in split order and completed decision minutes t ascending; maintain equity E, realized session loss L, soft-close state, and occupancy. While flat at t<15:30 and not halted, construct the time-t oracle choice universe solely from the referenced canonical intent law, commit at most one exact identity under the frozen tie-break, and then apply the referenced selected-contract-only t+1 recheck. A rejection logs the canonical event, opens no position, charges no premium or fee, realizes no PnL, permits no substitute, and returns to a later flat decision exactly as the canonical law specifies.
oracle_sequencing.threshold_independent_distributions: for the per-contract-minute distribution view (no serial account), causal time-t intent eligibility defines the opportunity universe. Successful t+1 recheck defines the separate realized-entry/reference-label population. Rejected intents remain explicit governed rows rather than disappearing or being renamed decision-time ineligible. D49 policy-ledger sequencing applies only to serial replay. FT2-05 reports all three populations and both rejection-rate denominators.

frozen_exit_rules.definition: for each horizon, choose exit-fill minute u* in W(t,h) with maximum executable bid B_(u*); the implied EXIT decision is v=u*-1 and realized fee-adjusted PnL uses B_(u*) against A_(t+1)
frozen_exit_rules.role: per-horizon opportunity ceiling; upper bound on what a perfect within-horizon exit could realize
frozen_exit_rules.censoring: if the horizon is censored near close, the max is taken over available minutes only

frozen_exit_rules.definition: value the still-open position once at the 15:55 forced-flat boundary bid; never substitute an earlier bid; if no executable boundary bid exists, option value is $0
frozen_exit_rules.role: the no-management baseline; what buying and letting it run to the close realizes

frozen_exit_rules.definition: choose the first exit-fill minute u* in W(t,remaining_session) with PnL$(u*)>0; implied EXIT decision is u*-1; if none, use the forced-flat boundary law
frozen_exit_rules.role: the take-the-first-green ceiling; ties directly to family (b) time-to-first-profit and bounds a maximally impatient exit
frozen_exit_rules.justification: authority family (b) defines time-to-first-real-profit; this oracle makes its realized-PnL ceiling explicit for the census

explicitly_not_included: any fixed stop / fixed target / fixed holding-time exit (the authority forbids fixed exits as truth; oracle rules are hindsight-transparent, not learned)
any exit that peeks at the eventual lifecycle model's selected exit
